title: Prune observability dependencies and introduce a lightweight span-shuttle for tracing efficiency
creator: Ava Patel
description: Background: Over time we've accumulated multiple OpenTelemetry exporters and helper libs across the runtime and edge services. This has increased binary size, cold-start allocations, and added cyclic deps that make minor upgrades (OTel SDK and logging libs) risky. The goal of this ticket is to (1) remove redundant heavy exporters and replace them with a tiny, in-process 'span-shuttle' shim that normalizes and forwards spans with minimal allocations; (2) prune or replace 3rd-party metric and logging transitive dependencies that blow up CI image sizes; (3) add a build-time flag to opt into full-featured exporters for debug builds only.
acceptance_criteria:
- Production build reduces observability-related binary size by >= 12% and peak RSS during startup by >= 15% on n1-standard test harness.
- End-to-end trace samples emitted via span-shuttle are OTLP-compatible and accepted by our collector with no loss of essential attributes for SLO debugging.
- No regression in request P50 latency (target: within 2% of baseline) under the continuous-batching load test.
- All removed exporters have documented migration notes and fallback plan in the Confluence doc.
- Feature gated behind runtime flag (RUNTIME_LIGHT_SPAN_SHUTTLE=true) and toggled via canary for 10% traffic before wide rollout.
design_notes:
Span-shuttle design: a tiny abstraction living in the runtime agent layer that accepts completed spans, performs lightweight normalization (string interning for common keys, drop of very high-cardinality attributes), then forwards to a single internal exporter pipeline. Key properties: low alloc path (pre-allocated buffer reused across requests), samplers unchanged (we respect parent/remote sampling decisions), OTLP wire compatibility preserved.
Dependency pruning: replace 'heavy-logger-x' with a lightweight shim that implements the subset we use (structured JSON, leveled). Remove redundant OTLP exporters from edge-worker images; use the span-shuttle to fan-out in the collector instead of in each binary.
Trade-offs: loses per-service custom exporter wiring (decided acceptable because collector-level routing covers most use-cases). Some vendor-specific metadata mapping will be centralized in the collector rather than emitted at source.
migration_plan:
1) Merge span-shuttle implementation behind feature flag. 2) Deploy to staging and run full regression/benchmark suite. 3) Canary deploy to 10% of runtime traffic with increased sampling to exercise span paths. 4) Monitor dashboards for errors, dropped spans, and SLO regressions for 48h. 5) If stable, increment canary to 50% then 100% over 72h. 6) Remove legacy exporters in a follow-up ticket after 2 weeks of stable telemetry.
Rollback: flip feature flag off and restart affected runtime pools. Collector accepts both old and new formats during migration window.
testing_and_benchmarks:
- Unit tests for span normalization and attribute reduction.
- Micro-benchmarks: allocation and time-per-span comparisons between old exporter path and span-shuttle.
- Integration tests against local OTLP collector and our QA tracing backend (trace-diff scripts).
- Load tests: continuous-batching trace generation at 1000 concurrent sequences for 30 minutes comparing P50/P95/P99 latencies and worker RSS.
- Canary monitoring: track span volume, span latency, error rate, CPU and memory per container, and request latency percentiles.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: Feature branch and internal review (now).
Phase 1: Merge behind flag to main; run nightly benchmarks.
Phase 2: Canary 10% (3 days) with synthetic load and active tracing.
Phase 3: 50% canary (2 days).
Phase 4: 100% for all runtime pools, then schedule follow-up to remove legacy exporters.
Communication: update #telemetry and #runtime-changes channels + triage doc in Confluence with rollback runbook.
blockers:
- Final compatibility test with vendor A's trace processor (they require service.version attr in a custom field). Work with SRE to map attributes in the collector during canary.
- CI image size budget gating currently flags any change to the agent image; need temporary exemption for benchmark PR.
- One downstream repo still depends on heavy-logger-x API; coordination needed to switch to shim.
